draft.title: Factors affecting photosynthesis
card: The rate of photosynthesis is how fast a plant makes glucose, and it can be measured by oxygen released or carbon dioxide taken up. Four factors set it: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, temperature and water availability.
As light intensity or carbon dioxide concentration rises, the rate rises at first. It then levels off, because another factor has become limiting, such as enzyme amount or the other input.
Temperature affects the enzymes involved, such as Rubisco. The rate rises with warmth up to an optimum, then falls as the enzymes lose their shape (denature).
Water is a reactant. When water is short, plants close their stomata to save it, which also limits carbon dioxide entering the leaf and so slows photosynthesis.
draft.remember: The factor in shortest supply limits the rate, and the rate stops rising once another factor limits it.

a.q: A graph shows the rate of photosynthesis rising with light intensity, then flattening out. What does the flat part show?
opts: Another factor is now limiting the rate
Light has stopped being needed at all
The enzymes have denatured from the light
The plant has run out of water to use
a.why: Once light is no longer the factor in shortest supply, more light cannot raise the rate, as something else such as carbon dioxide or temperature limits it. Denaturing would make the rate fall, not level off.
a.clue: Adding more of one input stops helping when something else is scarce.

b.q: During a dry spell, Lena's tomato plants wilt and photosynthesise more slowly, even though the sun is bright and the air has plenty of carbon dioxide. What best explains this?
opts: Stomata close, so less carbon dioxide enters the leaves
Bright light denatures chlorophyll in the leaves
Carbon dioxide in the air becomes too low to use
Rubisco makes more glucose when water is scarce
b.why: Water shortage makes the plant close its stomata, so carbon dioxide cannot enter easily even though the air has plenty. Outside carbon dioxide is not low, so the third option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about what closing stomata does to gas entry.

a.best: Another factor is now limiting the rate

b.best: Stomata close, so less carbon dioxide enters the leaves

The why calls the low-carbon-dioxide option 'the third option', but options are shown in random order (here it is first). It should name the option by its content.
The clue 'stops helping when something else is scarce' restates the right option ('Another factor is now limiting the rate'), so a student can match it without knowing the idea.

b.q: During a dry spell, Lena's tomato plants wilt and photosynthesise more slowly, even though the sun is bright and the air has plenty of carbon dioxide. What best explains this?
opts: Stomata close, so less carbon dioxide enters the leaves
Stomata open wider, so more water is lost from the leaves
